title: Falafel
description: Canned chickpeas bound with chickpea flour and an egg. The flour is what makes these forgiving — it takes up the residual moisture that otherwise has falafel collapsing in the pan.

ingredients.note: packed leaves — parsley, cilantro, or a mix

steps.heading: Oven Dry
steps.text: Drain and rinse both cans of chickpeas. Spread them in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Slip them into the 400°F oven next to the potatoes for just 10 minutes, until they look matte and dry. Remove and let cool for 5 minutes.

steps.heading: Blend
steps.text: Place the dried chickpeas, chopped yellow onion, minced garlic, packed parsley leaves, cumin, coriander, salt and black pepper into a food processor.

steps.heading: Pulse
steps.text: Pulse 10 to 12 times. The texture must look like coarse, wet sand — do not puree it into hummus.

steps.heading: Bind & Chill
steps.text: Transfer to a bowl. Stir in the chickpea flour and the beaten egg by hand until uniform — keep the flour out of the processor, or you will work the mixture into a paste. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes; the flour goes on taking up moisture while it rests.

steps.heading: Shape
steps.text: Gently form the cold mixture into 12 to 14 small, flattened patties, about 1.5 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick. They should hold their edges cleanly — if they slump, work in another tablespoon of chickpea flour and chill for another 10 minutes.

steps.heading: Pan-Fry
steps.text: Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the patties in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until a deep golden crust forms. Flip carefully with a thin spatula. Drain on paper towels.

notes: Chickpea flour rather than wheat: it is gluten-free, cheap, in most supermarkets and every Indian grocer, and being ground chickpeas it reinforces the flavour instead of muddying it. Fry these last, right before serving — they are only good hot and crisp.
